QF.id: Issue Management - General Obligations and Due Diligence_14

question.text: A rights issue closes on April 5. The basis of allotment is finalized on April 25, but the issue fails. The refund of money to applicants is made on May 1 (i.e., the refund date is May 1). By when must the final post-issue report be submitted?

answer.text: May 10 (15 days from allotment finalization on April 25)
May 16 (15 days from refund date on May 1)
May 8 (7 days from refund date on May 1)
April 20 (15 days from issue closure on April 5)

explanation.text: The Logic: For a rights issue that fails, the final post-issue report must be submitted within 15 days from the date of refund of money to the applicants. With the stem now fixing May 1 as the refund date, the deadline is May 1 + 15 days = May 16. The Trap: "May 10" anchors on the allotment-finalization date (April 25), but because the issue failed the trigger event moves to the refund date. "May 8" applies a 7-day public-issue timeline instead of the 15-day rights-issue timeline. "April 20" counts from issue closure, which is not the trigger for a failed rights issue. In the ambiguous original, "refunds are initiated on May 1" left it unclear whether May 1 was the date the refund process began or the date refunds were actually made; the audit flagged that the 15-day clock under SEBI ICDR runs from the refund of money date. Note: The original stem said refunds were "initiated" on May 1, which left it unclear whether May 1 itself was the refund date. The stem has been tightened to state explicitly that the refund of money is made on May 1, so the keyed answer of May 16 is now the unique outcome. Source: NISM-Series-IX Merchant Banking workbook, p.150.
